It is known that the mass of the cargo box is m0, the mass of the goods is m, and the truck moves to the left in uniform straight-line motion with speed v. When the goods are lifted to the position shown in the figure, which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The speed at which the cargo box moves upward is equal to vcosθ

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a truck uses a light cable passing over a smooth fixed pulley to lift a box of goods. It is known that the mass of the cargo box is m0, the mass of the goods is m, and the truck moves to the left in uniform straight-line motion with speed v. When the goods are lifted to the position shown in the figure, what is the speed at which the cargo box moves upward?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The speed at which the cargo box moves upward is equal to vcosθ
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the truck is on horizontal ground, and the arrow on the left is labeled with speed v and points to the left; the right end of the truck is connected to a light rope, and the rope first goes obliquely upward to the right around the fixed pulley above, then vertically downward to connect to the cargo box on the right. An angle θ is marked between the oblique rope and the horizontal dashed line above the truck, m0 is marked beside the cargo box, and m is marked on the goods inside the box. Reasoning: Let the length of the oblique rope from the truck connection point to the fixed pulley be l1, and the length of the vertical rope from the fixed pulley to the cargo box be l2. The light rope is inextensible and the fixed pulley is fixed, so l1+l2 is a constant. The truck connection point moves to the left with speed v, and the component of its velocity along the direction of the oblique rope that makes the oblique rope length increase is vcosθ, therefore dl1/dt = vcosθ. Since l1+l2 is unchanged, dl2/dt = -vcosθ, that is, the length of the vertical section of rope decreases at a rate of vcosθ, so the magnitude of the speed at which the cargo box moves upward is vcosθ.
